Proof. Define h:S→ℝ by h=(1/2)(f+g+|f−g|), where all the indicated operations are pointwise. We prove that h=f∨g by showing that the two functions have the same value at every element of S. Let s∈S be arbitrary, and put a=f(s) and b=g(s). By the definitions of the pointwise operations,

h(s)=(1/2)(f(s)+g(s)+|f(s)−g(s)|)=(1/2)(a+b+|a−b|).

Because the real numbers are totally ordered, either a≥b or a<b. If a≥b, then a−b≥0, so |a−b|=a−b, and max{a,b}=a. Consequently,

h(s)=(1/2)(a+b+a−b)=(1/2)(2a)=a=max{a,b}.

If a<b, then a−b<0, so |a−b|=−(a−b)=b−a, and max{a,b}=b. Consequently,

h(s)=(1/2)(a+b+b−a)=(1/2)(2b)=b=max{a,b}.

Thus in either case h(s)=max{f(s),g(s)}=(f∨g)(s). Since s was arbitrary, h and f∨g agree at every point of S; hence, by equality of functions,

f∨g=(1/2)(f+g+|f−g|). ∎
